source.title: Do Sparse Autoencoders Capture Concept Manifolds?
source.authors: Usha Bhalla; Thomas Fel; Can Rager; Sheridan Feucht; Tal Haklay; Daniel Wurgaft; S. Boppana; M. Kowal; Vasudev Shyam; Jack Merullo; Atticus Geiger; E. Lubana

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies sparse-autoencoder representations of manifolds and argues for interpreting groups of features rather than isolated directions. It does not test the neuron-pole audit, the InceptionV1 examples, attribution graphs, or the explanation-scoring claims in the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own results on SAE manifold representation, recorded below as related findings under versions ["none"]. These results do not measure the listed claim versions. Findings attributed to cited work are not included.
record.test_reason: The study trains SAEs on Llama3.1-8B layer-19 residual activations and characterizes how SAE dictionary features represent concept manifolds. It does not audit raw neuron poles, measure interpretable-neuron shares, revisit InceptionV1 neurons, build neuron-level attribution graphs, or score neuron explanations by activation simulation. Its remarks on automated interpretability concern SAE features and are argument, not a measured result on neurons.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors find that SAEs preserve manifold geometry only implicitly, tiling it across many localized, partially redundant features. They argue that interpretability should treat groups of features and geometric structures, not single directions, as units. They also propose an Ising-coupling method to recover such groups without supervision.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies SAE capture of manifolds, not the neuron-pole audit or explanation-evaluation procedures in the listed versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that SAE architecture and sparsity affect feature selectivity and reconstruction behavior.

fits_no_version.finding: On Llama3.1-8B layer 19, restricted R² from SAE features plateaus well beyond each manifold's ambient dimension. Features tile manifolds as localized, partially redundant detectors (the 'dilution' regime). An example is years features selective to the ones digit or the decade.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE features represent continuous concept manifolds through fragmented local tiling rather than compact subspaces, so single features give only a narrow view of the encoded concept.

fits_no_version.finding: Across SAE architectures, individual features align weakly, but the coordinate systems they induce on specific manifolds align strongly (App. B.3, Fig. 13).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: What is stable across SAE runs and architectures is manifold geometry, not individual features.

record.problems: The relevant SAE findings are mainly shown in figures, and the paper does not report uncertainty estimates for them. The experiments concern SAE features, not the neuron-pole explanations or attribution graphs in the listed versions.
record.rows_left_out: No results directly testing the listed versions were available. Other SAE architecture comparisons and synthetic-manifold results were not extracted as rows because they do not measure any listed version.

untested.parts: Qwen3-32B neuron-pole job shares; not studied.
Neuron interpretability shares across models, MoE, and scale; only Llama3.1-8B SAEs used.
InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron and recursive generalization; not examined.
Causes of messy neurons and how the interpretable share changes with tools and architecture; SAE architecture effects reported concern feature geometry, not neuron shares.
Neuron-based attribution graphs and their reconstruction error; not studied.
Whether activating-example explanations predict firing; not measured.
Simulation-based scoring of neuron explanations; not measured. The paper only argues that isolated-feature autointerp may fail or hallucinate meaning.

record.verdict_notes: This is about SAE features, not neurons, so no version is tested. One link worth noting for a researcher is the claim that local tiling resembles population coding, where a single unit covers a range of a concept's values. That is loosely related to V3/V6-style debates, but no neuron-level measurement is made.

versions.untested_parts: The Qwen3-32B neuron-pole audit shares and explanation testing on held-out activations.
Interpretable-neuron shares across models, architectures, and scale.
The InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron and recursive generalization.
The proposed causes of messy neurons and the interpretability-share estimates for InceptionV1-sized vision models.
Attribution graphs made from model neurons, behavioral explanation, and reconstruction error.
Whether explanations based on activating examples predict where a neuron fires.
Automated scoring of neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.

rows.subject: Llama3.1-8B
rows.operation_detail: Measured reconstruction of manifold contributions using increasing numbers of SAE decoder features.

conditions.value: manifold datasets described in Appendix B

rows.measure: Restricted R² as a function of the number of selected features.
rows.value: Variance explained grows with the number of restricted features but plateaus at a support size well beyond each manifold’s ambient dimension.
rows.note: The paper interprets this as manifolds being diluted across a larger, partially redundant set of SAE features rather than compactly captured. This measures SAE features, not neuron-pole interpretability or attribution-graph explanations.
rows.check: Measures restricted R² of SAE decoder features on manifold contributions, not neuron interpretability. Link to none is correct.

rows.subject: Llama3.1-8B
rows.operation_detail: Examined SAE feature activations as the value of a manifold concept varied.
rows.measure: Feature activation tuning curves across year values.
rows.value: Features show localized, smooth activation patterns with overlapping support; most SAEs learn features selective to the ones digit, activating periodically every 10 years, alongside features encoding the decade.
rows.note: This is evidence about SAE feature selectivity on a manifold, not a test of whether neuron poles have one or more main jobs.
rows.check: SAE feature tuning curves on the years manifold, not model neurons. Link to none is correct.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
